\section{Nonzero-image integral bound}\label{app:tail}

For the negative $j$th image, $j\ge1$, substitute
$u=2\pi j-\theta$ and use $|\sin\theta|\le1$.  Extending its integration
range yields a bound
\[
t e^{-(2j-1)^2\pi^2/(2t)}.
\]
For the positive $j$th image the analogous bound is
$t e^{-2j^2\pi^2/t}$.  In both sequences the ratio of consecutive bounds is
at most $e^{-4\pi^2/t}$.  Their sum is therefore at most $E(t)$ in
\eqref{eq:E}.

For the zero image, integration by parts gives
\[
\int_\rho^\infty\theta^2e^{-\theta^2/(2t)}\dd\theta
=t\rho e^{-\rho^2/(2t)}
+t\sqrt{\frac{\pi t}{2}}\operatorname{erfc}
\left(\frac{\rho}{\sqrt{2t}}\right).
\]
The elementary inequality
$\operatorname{erfc}(z)\le e^{-z^2}/(\sqrt\pi z)$ gives the first term inside
the brackets in \eqref{eq:tail}.  No denominator enclosure is needed because
character orthogonality proves the normalizing denominator is exactly one.
